title: Long-Term Effects of Environmental Lead on Erythropoietin Production in Young Adults: A Follow-Up Study of a Prospective Cohort in Kosovo.
ehr_evidence: From our prospective birth cohort study in Mitrovica (a mining town) and Pristina (a control town), Kosovo, from 1985 to 1998, we located and assessed blood lead concentration (BPb) and serum EPO in 101 participants (mean age 24.9 years) in 2011.
summary: A follow-up of a prospective birth cohort in Kosovo assessed 101 young adults (mean age 24.9 years) for the association between prenatal, early childhood, and concurrent blood lead exposure and serum erythropoietin (EPO) concentration.
key_findings: When adjusted for hemoglobin as a continuous variable, the relationship between log BPb and log serum EPO became significant (estimated β = 0.19; 95% CI 0.06, 0.31).
A simple unadjusted linear regression relating log BPb to log serum EPO found no significant relationship (estimated β = 0.05; 95% CI −0.09, 0.20).

Significant positive associations were found between cumulative BPb (AUC between birth and age 2, ages 2–4, and ages 4–7) and EPO, but the estimated associations diminished with child age after adjustment for Hgb.
No association was found between cumulative BPb between ages 7 and 12 and EPO, though the sign of the association changed from hyperproduction to hypoproduction of EPO.
Mean serum EPO was significantly higher in Mitrovica (10.99 mIU/ml) than Prishtina (8.49 mIU/ml) (P < 0.04).
The association was stronger in anemic subjects (Hgb < 12.5 g/dl; β = 0.41; 95% CI 0.13, 0.70) than in non-anemic subjects (β = 0.05; 95% CI −0.10, 0.20).
captured_features: Cumulative lead exposure (area under the curve)
study_design: Prospective cohort (follow-up of a birth cohort)
population: 101 young adults (mean age 24.9 years) from a prospective birth cohort in Mitrovica (lead-exposed) and Prishtina (unexposed), Kosovo
limitations: Only 20% of the original cohort was followed up (101 of 574).
A 12.5-year gap between the last childhood BPb measurements and the single EPO measure.
EPO was measured only once per participant, so results may be affected by inter-assay variability.
The sample oversampled highly exposed children.
No bone marrow biopsy was performed.
No liver function tests were included.
Results may not be generalizable to populations with lower lead exposure or to other settings.
data_availability_statement: All pertinent data are in our study files and can be made available upon request.
